story: admin login and authentication  screen test cases

result.feature_understanding: The admin login and authentication screen lets administrators sign in so they can access the admin dashboard and manage the system. A critical rule is that any attempt to open an admin URL without a valid session must redirect the user to the login page. This screen connects to the POST /api/admin/auth/login (and related auth) endpoints to verify credentials. The biggest risk is that the authentication check could fail, allowing unauthorized access or keeping a session alive past its timeout. Test also needs to confirm that an idle admin session expires and the user is sent back to the login screen.

failure_path_tests.title: API timeout: POST /api/admin/auth/login exceeds SLA
failure_path_tests.description: Simulate POST /api/admin/auth/login taking longer than the SLA threshold (e.g. 30 s). Verify the client receives a meaningful timeout error and the operation does not partially commit.
steps: Configure POST /api/admin/auth/login to respond after 30 s (mock/stub)
Trigger the feature flow
Verify the caller receives HTTP 504 or an explicit timeout error
Verify no partial data was written to the database
Verify a retry or circuit-breaker mechanism activates if configured
failure_path_tests.expected_result: Caller gets a safe timeout error; no partial state change; circuit breaker trips after N failures

failure_path_tests.title: Circuit breaker opens after repeated failures on /api/admin/auth/login
failure_path_tests.description: Repeatedly fail the downstream dependency to trigger the circuit breaker. Verify open-state fast-fail behaviour and eventual half-open recovery.
steps: Cause /api/admin/auth/login to return 500 for 5 consecutive calls
Verify the circuit breaker moves to OPEN state
Verify subsequent calls fail fast (< 100 ms) without hitting the dependency
Wait for the cooldown window, then send one request
Verify the circuit breaker enters HALF-OPEN and allows the probe request
Verify recovery to CLOSED state on a successful probe
failure_path_tests.expected_result: Circuit breaker opens, fast-fails, and recovers correctly

failure_path_tests.title: admin login and authentication screen test: DB failure mid-transaction rolls back cleanly
failure_path_tests.description: Simulate a DB constraint violation or connection drop mid-transaction. Verify the entire operation rolls back and no event is published.
steps: Begin the feature operation
Inject a DB failure (constraint violation or connection timeout) after the first INSERT
Verify the DB transaction is fully rolled back
Verify NO domain event was published to the message broker
Verify the API returns a 500 with a safe error message (no SQL in response)
failure_path_tests.expected_result: Full rollback; no partial data; no spurious event published; safe error response

failure_path_tests.title: Duplicate POST /api/admin/auth/login request is idempotent
failure_path_tests.description: Send the same POST /api/admin/auth/login request twice with an identical idempotency key. Verify the second call returns the same result without creating a duplicate record or publishing a second event.
steps: Send POST /api/admin/auth/login with idempotency key 'KEY-001'
Verify the first call succeeds and creates the resource
Send the identical POST /api/admin/auth/login again with the same 'KEY-001' key
Verify the second call returns the same response (200/201) without a new DB record
Verify only ONE domain event was published total
failure_path_tests.expected_result: Second call is a no-op; exactly one DB record; exactly one event published

reasons: Authentication data (credentials, tokens) is highly sensitive (+0.20)
Multiple unauthenticated endpoints (login, refresh, me) increase attack surface (+0.15)
Integration of 3+ APIs (login, refresh, me) adds complexity (+0.15)
risk_areas.failure_propagation: If authentication fails, admins cannot access any admin UI, affecting all admin users and downstream services that rely on a valid auth token.
Login failure blocks admin access, halting all admin operations and any actions requiring admin privileges.

reasons: Refresh deals with auth tokens, which are security‑critical (+0.20)
Unauthenticated endpoint processes refresh token input (+0.15)
risk_areas.failure_propagation: Refresh failure invalidates the session, causing admins to be logged out and interrupting ongoing admin tasks.

reasons: Unauthenticated call with token input adds attack surface (+0.15)
risk_areas.failure_propagation: If /me fails, UI cannot display admin profile, causing errors in components that rely on user information.

reasons: Handles personal email addresses for password recovery (+0.20)
risk_areas.failure_propagation: Failure prevents admins from initiating password recovery, leading to possible lockout of admin accounts.

reasons: Processes new admin passwords, a highly sensitive operation (+0.20)
Unauthenticated endpoint receives reset token and new password (+0.15)
risk_areas.failure_propagation: Failure blocks password changes, potentially leaving compromised accounts unmitigated.

reasons: Invalidates session tokens, critical for security (+0.20)
Unauthenticated call may be invoked without proper auth (+0.15)
risk_areas.failure_propagation: Logout failure may leave stale sessions active, increasing risk of unauthorized access after admin attempts to sign out.
